title: Semantic Units tiered pricing pilot + enterprise QSA alignment
creator: Anika Patel
description: Context: Customers using embeddings + reranking report unpredictable per-request economics when mixing many small calls with bulk batch jobs. Sales asks for clearer enterprise packaging and bulk discounts to close committed contracts; legal/compliance asks that pricing changes be reflected in contract language and the Security Questionnaire (QSA) where cost/usage terms are surfaced. Goal: design and validate a tiered pricing pilot that introduces a per-semantic-unit baseline plus batch slabs for high-volume calls, while delivering clear contract language and QSA guidance for Enterprise deals.
proposal_summary: Introduce 'Semantic Unit' as the billed unit (1 vector dimension unit normalized) and offer a three-way pricing experiment: 1) baseline per-semantic-unit on pay-as-you-go; 2) committed monthly slab discounts (3 tiers: 100M, 1B, 10B SU/month) with stepped unit price; 3) micro-batch credits: bundle-of-calls discount for short high-frequency requests (applies to per-request batching up to 256 vectors). Pilot to run with a set of 6 customers (mix of PLG and sales-led) and internal traffic to measure elasticity, blocking risks, and billing infra changes.
pricing_options: Option A - Simple per-SU: $0.00008 / SU PAYG. Option B - Slabed Commit: Tier1 100M SU @ $0.00006, Tier2 1B SU @ $0.000045, Tier3 10B SU @ $0.000032 with minimum monthly commitment and 6-month contract. Option C - Hybrid with micro-batch credits: same per-SU baseline but purchase 'micro-batch credits' (1 credit = 100 calls up to 16 vectors) at blended 25% discount. Rationale: cover common enterprise ask for predictability (Commits) and improve PLG conversion via easy batch credits. Proposed nominal discount bands chosen to target 20-60% unit reduction at scale to align with cost-of-serving projections.
experiment_plan: Cohort selection: 4 existing customers (1 enterprise, 2 scale-ups, 1 high-volume PLG) + 2 internal Redwood pilots (console analytics, batch eval pipeline). Duration: 8 weeks. Hypotheses: H1 - Commit tiers increase average contract size by >= 2x for enterprise customers; H2 - Micro-batch credits reduce per-call latency regressions by <5% while improving revenue retention for PLG. Success metrics: ARR delta, conversion rate to commit offers, average revenue per active SU, unit cost delta on infra. Runbook: pricing toggles feature-flagged by customer; finance tracks realized ARPU; legal signs updated SOW and pricing exhibits; billing mocks validated against synthetic traffic first.
telemetry_metrics: To capture: total SU consumed per customer/day, SU per call histogram, batch size distribution, percent of calls qualifying for micro-batch credits, revenue per SU, churn/renewals post-offer, conversion funnel (offer viewed -> accepted), average latency by batch bracket, cache-hit correlation with SU billed. Dashboards: create 'pricing-experiments' dashboard in Console with per-customer and aggregate views.
engineering_work: Billing: add 'semantic_unit' meter to billing pipeline, support slab pricing and credit redemption in payments engine, backfill 90 days for cohort customers for A/B comparisons. SDK/API: annotate responses with 'billing_breakdown' field when feature flag enabled. Runtime: ensure prefix/KV caching does not double-bill across micro-batch credits. Required PRs: billing-service#4123, usage-collector#289, api-sdk#198. Estimate: 5 sprint points for core billing change + 3 for SDK annotations + 2 for infra dashboards.
contract_qsa_changes: Legal to produce an updated pricing exhibit template (SOW Pricing Exhibit v2) and a short QSA section that maps pricing terms to security/compliance questions where relevant (e.g., 'Does your pricing require transfer of PII for billing?' -> No; 'Is usage data exported to third parties?' -> Only to payment processors with contractual safeguards). Action items: (1) Legal to draft clause for commit credits rollover/forfeiture; (2) Security to sign-off on telemetry retention windows used for billing; (3) Sales ops to standardize discount approval matrix for commits >25%.
rollout_timeline: Week 0-2: finalize pricing bands and legal exhibits; implement feature flags. Week 3-4: implement billing meters and SDK annotations; run internal smoke tests. Week 5-8: onboard pilot customers, monitor dashboards daily, collect qualitative feedback. Week 9: review pilot outcomes and decide scaling or iteration. Target GA decision by 2026-05-01.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Billing pipeline records 'semantic_unit' metric and produces invoice-level rollups matching synthetic ground truth within 0.5% error. 2) At least 4 pilot customers complete a 6-week trial with data collected. 3) Legal approves Pricing Exhibit v2 and QSA addendum. 4) Finance approves modeled unit economics (breakeven and target margin >= 35% at Tier2). 5) No unresolved security blocker from Security team.
